([[Woodstock, Virginia]]) | college = [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] (2013–2017) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * [[List of U.S. men's college basketball national player of the year awards|Consensus National college player of the year]] ([[2016-17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017]]) * [[Bob Cousy Award]] (2017) * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2017 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2017]]) * [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] (2017) * First-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2017) * 2× Second-team All-Big 12 (2015, 2016) * Big 12 All-Defensive Team (2016) * [[Summer Universiade|World University Games]] MVP ([[Basketball at the 2015 Summer Universiade – Men's tournament|2015]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men’s [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|{{USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[Summer Universiade]]}} {{MedalGold| [[Basketball at the 2015 Summer Universiade|2015 Gwangju]] | [[United States men's national basketball team|Team competition]]}} }} '''Frank Leo Mason III''' (born April 3, 1994) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[University of Kansas]], where he was the starting [[point guard]] for the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Jayhawks]]. For the 2016–17 season, he was named National Player of the Year by all of the major national player awards, making him consensus national player of the year. The awards are the [[John R. Wooden Award]], [[CBS Sports Network|CBS Sports National Player of the Year]],{{cite news |last=Norlander |first=Matt |date=March 29, 2017 |title=Kansas' Frank Mason parlays consistency, efficiency into CBS Player of the Year honor |url=http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/kansas-frank-mason-parlays-consistency-efficiency-into-cbs-player-of-the-year-honor/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |location=[[New York City]], [[New York (state)|New York]] |access-date=April 10, 2017}} the USA Today, the [[Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|Sporting News Player of the Year]], [[Associated Press College Basketball Player of the Year|Associated Press Player of the Year]], [[Naismith College Player of the Year]], [[Oscar Robertson Trophy]], and [[NABC Player of the Year]].{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=April 2, 2017 |title=KU’s Frank Mason adds to award haul with NABC player of year|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article142336589.html |work=[[The Kansas City Star]] |location=[[Kansas City, Missouri]] |access-date=April 3, 2017}} He was also a consensus All-American selection for his senior season at Kansas.[http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article141222033.html Kansas' Frank Mason III is AP Player of the Year, unanimous All-American Selection], Kansas City Star, March 28, 2017. ==Early life== Mason grew up in [[Petersburg, Virginia]] and went to [[Petersburg High School (Virginia)]]. He scored 1,901 points in his four-year career at Petersburg, which is the second highest scoring total in school history behind NBA Hall of Famer [[Moses Malone]].{{cite web|title=Frank Mason III - 2013-14 Men's Basketball|url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=5200|website=KU Athletics|accessdate=April 3, 2017}} Mason had originally signed to attend [[Towson University]] in [[Towson, Maryland]] during his senior year, but he lost his eligibility after failing a government class.{{cite web|last1=Shaffer|first1=Jonas|title=A failing grade kept Kansas point guard Frank Mason III away from Towson|url=http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/baltimore-sports-blog/bal-a-failing-grade-kept-kansas-point-guard-frank-mason-iii-away-from-towson-20160324-story.html|website=The Baltimore Sun|accessdate=March 21, 2017}} Mason attended [[Massanutten Military Academy]] in [[Woodstock, Virginia]] to make up for the failing grade in government. After being discovered playing the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit by Kansas Assistant Coach [[Kurtis Townsend]], Mason was offered a scholarship by the [[University of Kansas]].{{cite web|last1=Moore|first1=C.J.|title=HOW FRANK MASON WENT FROM UNWANTED RECRUIT TO THE KANSAS JAYHAWKS' LEADING MAN|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2382892-how-frank-mason-went-from-unwanted-recruit-to-the-kansas-jayhawks-leading-man|website=Bleacher Report|accessdate=March 21, 2017}} ==College career== As a sophomore at Kansas, he was a second team All Big 12 selection.{{cite web|title=Sooners' Hield Leads All-Big 12 Men's Basketball Honors|url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=209934691|website=[[Big 12 Conference]]|accessdate=May 17, 2015|date=March 8, 2015}} He averaged 12.6 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 3.9 assists per game as a sophomore, an increase from the 5.5 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game he averaged as a freshman.{{cite web|title=Frank Mason III|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/frank-mason-player|website=[[Fox Sports]]|accessdate=August 10, 2015}} During his junior season, Mason averaged 12.9 points and 4.6 assists and was named to the Big 12 All-Defensive Team. During his senior season, Mason took on more of a leadership role on the Kansas team, becoming the first player in Big 12 history to average 20 points and 5 assists a game during the regular season.{{cite web|title=Frank Mason III becomes the first player in big 12 history to average 20 points and 5 assists per game for a season|url=https://www.reddit.com/r/CollegeBasketball/comments/5xo6yk/frank_mason_iii_becomes_the_first_player_in_big/|website=[[Reddit]]|accessdate=March 21, 2017}} His regular season culminated in receiving multiple awards. He was unanimously selected as the Big 12 Player of the Year, averaging 20.5 points and 5.1 assists in the regular season.{{cite web|title=KU’s Frank Mason, Bill Self are Big 12 player, coach of the year|url=http://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article136592088.html|website=[[The Kansas City Star]]|accessdate=March 21, 2017}} He was also consensus first team All-American selection, the NCAA leading 29th 1st team selection in Kansas basketball history.{{cite web|title=Mason earns Consensus All-America First Team distinction|url=http://www.kuathletics.com/news/2017/3/28/mens-basketball-mason-earns-consensus-all-america-first-team-distinction.aspx|website=KUAthletics.com}} He was awarded multiple player of the year awards including [[Associated Press|AP Player of the Year]],{{cite web|title=Kansas' Frank Mason III is AP Player of the Year, unanimous All-America
